subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async lifecycle primitive for drain/cancel semantics, and should that contract live in core gateway/agent runtime or the plugin SDK?
rationale: Current main already has localized cleanup helpers and targeted fixes, so the remaining work is an API ownership and shutdown-semantics decision rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner-approved design that names the API boundary, shutdown ordering, timeout behavior, and representative migrations before implementation.

options.title: Continue localized helpers only
options.body: Treat the existing focused Feishu, embedded-runner, channel, and plugin cleanup helpers as the preferred model and close only after a maintainer says no shared primitive is wanted.

options.title: Defer until a new concrete failure
options.body: Leave broad consolidation unscheduled and require a fresh reproducible lifecycle bug before expanding core or SDK API surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner-approved design that names the API boundary, shutdown ordering, timeout behavior, and representative migrations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision crosses plugin SDK/channel lifecycle and embedded-runner helper surfaces where recent history points to steipete.
